title: On the minimum size of maximal $k$-wise intersecting families
summary: A family $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of $[n] := \{1,2,\ldots, n\}$ is called maximal $k$-wise intersecting if every collection of at most $k$ members of $\mathcal{F}$ has a non-empty intersection, and adding any other set to $\mathcal{F}$ breaks this property. An old question by Erdős and Kleitman from 1974 asks for the minimum size of a maximal $k$-wise intersecting family. The case $k = 3$ is known for all sufficiently large $n$, but the problem remains open for all $k \geqslant 4$.
